answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a stake-bonded ledge: every identity locks a small bond before it may quote, bid, or vouch. Identities then earn nectar — a slow-drip reputation compounding only through delivered, peer-reviewed work — so freshly minted sockpuppets stay resource-poor. Each job is signed into a public work fable, a chronological record any peer can audit. Forging a thousand fakes means locking a thousand bonds and re-earning nectar from zero each time, so the attack costs more than honest work, and clones fail because stake, nectar history, and fable will not line up.
